title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap & Pricing (2026-03-04)
author: Avery Chen
body:
## Summary
This document bundles the product overview, high-level PRD, design specification, roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging guidance, and release notes for the Unified Inference initiative (Q2 2026 deliverables). It describes customer problem statements, prioritized requirements, an implementation sketch that ties into the Redwood serving runtime, go-to-market packaging and pricing guidance, and an operational rollout plan.

## Background & Opportunity
Redwood's customers are standardizing on LLM-based product capabilities but face fragmentation across deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private). Customers ask for a single configuration and policy surface that provides: predictable latency, straightforward cost controls, a consistent API, and easy migration between deployment modes. Unified Inference aims to reduce operational burden for customers and expand Redwood's TAM by simplifying product adoption for platform teams and enterprise customers.

## Personas
- Software/ML Engineers: want stable APIs, predictable latency/cost, and simple model pinning.
- Platform Engineers: want programmatic deploys, autoscaling policies, and observability hooks.
- Procurement/Finance: want clear billing tiers and cost predictability.

## Goals (success criteria)
1. Single API/config surface across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
2. Model routing and fallback policies available as first-class config.
3. Provide cost controls (per-route budgets, batching/quantization suggestions) that reduce per-token cost by >=20% for targeted workloads.
4. Shipping observability and rollout tooling sufficient for SREs and platform teams (token-level cost breakdown, per-model latency SLOs, rollout metrics).

## Non-Goals
- This release does not include new model training infrastructure or model development workflows.
- Does not include advanced policy engines for content moderation beyond existing safety filters.

## High-level Product Requirements (PRD)
(Each requirement includes rationale and acceptance criteria)
1) Unified API surface
- Rationale: Reduce customer integration effort and enable seamless migration.
- Requirement: A single REST/gRPC/SDK interface that supports text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking with deployment-agnostic configuration.
- Acceptance: Customer can switch a route between Hosted and Dedicated with no code changes and validated SLOs in a staging test.

2) Model Routing & Fallbacks
- Rationale: Keep services available during capacity constraints and enable cost-latency tradeoffs.
- Requirement: Policy-driven routing by latency, cost, region, and model health; automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Acceptance: Route policy configuration page + API returns chosen route metadata in response headers; fallback exercised in chaos test.

3) Cost Controls & Optimize Suggestions
- Requirement: Per-route budgets, autosuggest batching and quantization profiles, and estimation API for per-token unit economics.
- Acceptance: Suggestion engine produces a recommended batching/config profile and estimated 90th percentile cost delta; UI surfaces actionable changes.

4) Observability & Rollouts
- Requirement: Per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, model-level latency SLOs, rollout primitives (canary, A/B, automatic rollback).
- Acceptance: Console has dashboard widgets for new route; rollout can be configured and executed via UI + API with rollback on SLO breach.

5) Private Deployment Parity
- Requirement: Feature parity (config and API) for Private deployments except where cloud-managed features are explicitly blocked by customer isolation.
- Acceptance: Private deployment test harness demonstrates identical API and config semantics; documented exceptions included.

## Design Spec (implementation sketch)
### Architecture overview
- Control plane: Redwood control-plane (hosted) manages config, model catalog, routing policies, and rollout state. For Private customers, a local control-plane proxy syncs configs with customer-managed control plane components.
- Data plane: Serving runtime runs on GPU clusters; supports runtime selection of quantized kernels, prefix caching, and continuous batching.
- Routing layer: Service that evaluates routing policies and selects a target deployment instance (hosted/dedicated/private) and model variant. Exposes metrics for decisions.

### Key services and contracts
- API Gateway (redwood-api): Unified REST/gRPC surface; injects route metadata and exposes route config API.
- Router Service (router-svc): Evaluates policies in ~1ms median decision time; supports pluggable policy evaluators.
- Suggestion Engine (optimize-svc): Offline and online suggestion engine that consumes token distributions to recommend batching/quantization.
- Rollout Controller (rollout-svc): Orchestrates canaries/A-Bs and monitors SLOs.

### Data model & configuration
We store route config as flat key-value fields: route_id, default_model, allowed_models (list), routing_policy_id, budget_usd_per_hour, rollout_strategy.
Example route configuration table (CSV-like):
- route_id,default_model,allowed_models,routing_policy_id,budget_usd_per_hour,rollout_strategy
- retail-chat-frontend,redwood-13b-8bit,[redwood-13b-8bit;redwood-13b-4bit],latency-first,12.00,canary-5pct

### API changes / examples
- POST /v1/routes -> create route with fields above.
- GET /v1/routes/{id}/suggestions -> returns batching/quantization recommendations (JSON in response body).
- Response header X-Redwood-Route: route_id and X-Redwood-Fallback: model_variant if fallback used.

### SLOs and performance targets
- Route policy decision latency: p50 < 2ms, p99 < 10ms.
- Inference latency overhead for routing layer: <= 5ms added p50.
- Suggestion generation: online suggestions updated hourly, offline batch weekly.

## Requirements Matrix (prioritized)
Priority P0: Unified API, model routing, per-route budgeting, rollout primitives, private parity tests.
Priority P1: Suggestion engine, detailed token-level cost UI, advanced rollout strategies (progressive traffic shaping).
Priority P2: Multi-tenant quota auto-healing, policy marketplace integrations.

## Roadmap & Themes (Q2-Q4 2026)
- Q2 2026 (MVP): Unified API + basic routing + per-route budgets + canary rollout + console widgets + Private parity tests.
- Q3 2026: Suggestion engine launch, autoscaling policy hooks, expanded observability (traces + token-level cost drilldown).
- Q4 2026: Advanced rollout strategies, marketplace integrations (partners), and expanded pricing/packaging for enterprise reserved capacity.

Milestones and owners:
- M1 (2026-04-15): API and route CRUD endpoints completed \u2014 Owner: eng-developer-experience.
- M2 (2026-05-20): Router service MVP + fallback logic + chaos tests \u2014 Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
- M3 (2026-06-10): Console widgets + rollout controller integration \u2014 Owner: eng-platform.

## Pricing & Packaging Notes
Principles:
- Keep pricing simple for self-serve customers; provide granular reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated and Private.
- Surface cost controls as additive value (Optimize suggestions part of Redwood Optimize add-on).

Suggested packaging tiers:
1) Starter (Hosted) \u2014 Pay-as-you-go. Includes unified API, basic routing, 30 days of observability retention.
2) Business (Hosted + Dedicated eligibility) \u2014 Committed usage discount (10\u201325% depending on commit). Includes rollout primitives, per-route budgets, and priority support.
3) Enterprise (Dedicated + Private) \u2014 Reserved capacity contracts, extended retention, SAML/SCIM, encrypted control-plane connectors, professional services.

Add-ons:
- Redwood Optimize (suggestions & regressions): flat monthly + usage-based component.
- Premium Observability: extended retention and custom dashboards.

Example pricing assumptions (internal guidance):
- Incremental cost for unified routing and rollout features: operational overhead ~0.2\u20130.5% of serving costs.
- Expected uplift in average deal size for Business/Enterprise tiers: 15\u201330%.

## Release Notes (2026-03-04 release)
Highlights:
- Unified API: Route CRUD endpoints and SDK support for route binding and config.
- Router Service MVP: latency-first routing policy and automatic fallback to quantized model variants.
- Per-route budgets: UI + API for budget creation and enforcement (soft stop + notification).
- Rollout primitives in Console: canary and manual A/B with automatic rollback on SLO breaches.

Migration notes for customers:
1) New routes are created via POST /v1/routes. Existing endpoints remain compatible for the initial migration period.
2) To enable fallback behavior, add allowed_models to route config.
3) Customers on Private should run the new sync agent (private-control-proxy v1.2) to receive config parity.

Known limitations and workarounds:
- Suggestion engine is not enabled in this MVP; manual batching config still accepted.
- In heavy cross-region failover, telemetry may lag by up to 30s; increase alert window accordingly.

## Rollout Plan
1) Internal dogfooding (2 weeks): enable feature for platform team and 3 internal apps; collect telemetry.
2) Beta customers (4 weeks): invite 6 select customers (combination of hosted and dedicated) with onboarding runbook.
3) Gradual public launch (2 phases): start with opt-in for new routes, then default enable after 6 weeks of stable metrics.

Runbook highlights for incidents:
- If router-svc exhibits elevated p99 decision latency > 50ms: divert traffic to a static routing table and scale router-svc nodes.
- If rollout controller triggers rollback, follow automated rollback then open postmortem ticket (owner: eng-platform).

## Success metrics
- Adoption: 30% of new Hosted routes use unified routing within 3 months.
- Cost savings: average 20% per-token unit cost reduction for pilot customers using Optimize suggestions.
- Reliability: No customer-facing downtime attributable to routing logic in 99.95% of routes across first 3 months post-launch.

## Dependencies
- eng-serving-runtime: stable fallback model variants and quantized kernels.
- eng-infra: autoscaling policies and dedicated capacity enforcement.
- eng-platform: rollout controller and console widgets.
- Security & Compliance: approval for Private control-plane sync design.

## Appendix: Acceptance test checklist
1) Route CRUD APIs validated with unit and e2e tests.
2) Router service chaos tests simulating instance loss and model variant exhaustion.
3) Private parity tests syncing config with private-control-proxy v1.2.
4) Console rollout test with auto-rollback on SLO breach.

For questions or to request early access to the Beta program, contact the product owner or sign up at the internal beta tracker.
